text:
Lois Agnello wanted to try a 3D-printed hand. At her school in Port Macquarie, Australia, that idea became a project she could shape alongside her classmates.
With teacher Lloyd Godson’s guidance and an open-source design from Free 3D Hands, the students worked through printing, assembly, and repeated adjustments. They spent lunch breaks on the project over several months, learning that a useful design takes more than pressing “print.”
